reading_workflow.detail: The whole page was inspected once for layout and both prepared native-dimension overlapping halves were read once line by line, including all agreed words and signs. The 38 baselines comprise 22 body/display/number/insertion baselines, twelve oblique upper-note lines and four lower-note lines. The signature diagram, its two endpoints, shaft, head and chi label were inspected separately. Every saved first crop was viewed once; the rotated crops are reused without recropping. No OCR, external research or TeX compilation was used.
reading_workflow.crop_method: All change rows cite the original saved rectangles, including the unrotated native coordinates for the two rotated crops. Same-dimension quality95 JPEG proxies were used for display only. Second boxes may be smaller native subrectangles.
reading_workflow.mathematical_scope: One explicit finite sign-group computation was performed for the connectedness caveat; it does not choose a reading or prove the full groupoid theory.

notes.text: The sheet defines an oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid using compact oriented surfaces with boundary and isotopy classes of orientation-preserving isomorphisms. Its immediate variant permits homeomorphisms without necessarily preserving orientation. This report records those definitions, not a separate verification of the full theory.

If disconnected surfaces and all homeomorphisms are admitted literally, two oriented disks provide four componentwise sign states. Independent reflections form a four-element subgroup whose orientation-preserving sign state is only (++). Enumerating its maps to {±1} gives four homomorphisms with kernel sizes 4,2,2,2; none has that singleton kernel. This conditional obstruction supports the margin’s connectedness caveat. It does not decide the doubtful first word or alter the source formula.

The upper note is transcribed beside the first definition, its physical position. The loop/apostrophe-like marks immediately left of its final orienté belong to the crossing body phrase l’orientation; they are not added as l’orienté or as the end of an expanded groupoïde.
